reason: The request handler calls a helper that reaches into the store through the service's private _store attribute, so it talks to the store rather than the application only.
LendingService ignores the injected notifier and creates its own notifier class internally, so lending no longer notifies through the injected notifier.
The request handler imports and instantiates the in-memory adapter InMemoryLoanStore, so handlers depend on adapters and talk to the store directly.
The application imports the OutboxNotifier adapter and creates it in its constructor, replacing the injected notifier and reversing the layer dependency.
The memory store resets loan.returned to False on add, which is a state change outside Loan.close but does not close a loan, so no graded requirement is broken.
OutboxNotifier.send now takes (text, recipient), so it no longer satisfies the Notifier port's send(member, text) signature.
The handler uses a new response helper module that touches neither the store nor adapters, which is a restructuring that keeps the architecture intact.
